hero.title:
Mastery,
since 1995
hero.lede: From the counter Metin Hançerlioğlu opened in Erdemli to this day: yufka stretched by hand, pistachio, and a measure that has not changed.

philosophy.label: Philosophy
philosophy.statement: We do not make sweets. We keep a promise made in 1995 — that every sheet of yufka be stretched thin enough to read the light through it, and that nothing leave the counter unless it can carry our name.

legacy.caption: Metin Hançerlioğlu, at the marble counter, Erdemli.
legacy.title: The hands it began with
legacy.p1: In 1995, in Erdemli, Metin Hançerlioğlu opened a room four trays wide. A marble counter, a pan hammered by hand, and a belief that yufka could be stretched until the light passed through it.
legacy.p2: He refused shortcuts the way other people refuse a debt. Butter was clarified at dawn, and the pistachio was opened piece by piece. A torn sheet was not sold; it was set aside. The house was built on what it was willing to throw away.
legacy.p3: The years passed. The counter is the same stone. The measure has not moved.
legacy.alt: Hançerlioğlu — Metin Hançerlioğlu at the marble counter of the Erdemli workshop

heritage.title: Two stops
heritage.intro: One is the year the counter was set. The other is the year the house reached the place and the scale it has today.
heritage.firstText: Metin Hançerlioğlu opens the door in Erdemli. One marble, one pan, four trays. The measure is set that day, and it is never argued again.
heritage.secondText: The house reaches the scale it has today. The workshop on Erdemoğlu Boulevard opens; katmer, künefe and baklava are gathered under one roof, to the same measure.
heritage.alt1995: Hançerlioğlu — Metin Hançerlioğlu at the counter he founded in 1995

craft.title: The art of the sweet
craft.intro: Three disciplines. Each has its own hour, its own metal, and its own quiet.
craft.baklavaText: Forty sheets of yufka, each thinned until a printed page could be read through it, layered with butter clarified at dawn and chosen Antep pistachio. It bakes in copper, rests, and meets the syrup at the difference in heat that keeps the leaves apart.
craft.kuneText: Kadayıf as fine as a hair is laid around unsalted cheese drawn that morning, and turned in hand-hammered copper over an open fire. The master watches the sound, not the clock: when the sizzle drops half a tone, the plate is finished. There is no moment after.
craft.katmerText: It is thrown into the air, the width of a table, until it is nearly transparent, then closed over water-buffalo cream and coarsely ground pistachio. Katmer belongs to the first light. It is not held, not reheated, not sent out. It is eaten where it is made.
craft.quote: “Sugar is cheap. Time is not. We sell the second.”
craft.altBaklava: Hançerlioğlu — a tray of pistachio baklava, forty leaves
craft.altKune: Hançerlioğlu — künefe, the cheese pulling strand by strand

house.title: Still here, still deliberate
house.text: The workshop on Erdemoğlu Boulevard keeps the hour set in 1995. The shutters go up at four. The marble is cold. The first tray comes out before the street wakes — leaf by leaf.

visit.label: Visit
visit.title: Visit
visit.lede: The shutters rise before the city does. Come for the first tray, while the marble is still cold, or once the copper is already on the fire. The door is the one that opened in 1995.

cover.lede: Erdemli does not claim to have invented these sweets. It inherited them and has not let them go. Below is the whole practice of the house — leaf, strand, fire and cold — in the order the day builds them, and as it builds them.

catnav.label: Index
catnav.note:
Each work opens onto its own story.
Choose a name to read it.

cat.katmerNote: The dough is thrown into the air until it is thin enough to be read through a table. Katmer belongs to the hour before the city wakes; every form below is a separate answer to the same fold.
cat.kuneNote: Hammered copper over an open fire, and cheese drawn that morning. The master watches the sound, not the clock: when the sizzle drops half a tone, the plate is finished.
cat.kadayifNote: The strand of the künefe is parted from the cheese and left to stand on its own. Butter, pistachio and patience. There is nothing else to hide behind.
cat.baklavaNote: Forty leaves on the tray, each opened until a printed page could be read through it. The house has never changed that number, and it has never been asked to.
cat.iceNote: Salep and mastic are turned slowly enough that the result is taken with a knife, not a scoop. The cold room is the only place in the workshop the fire never reaches.
cat.kaymakNote: A single entry, because there is a single method. Everything in this catalogue that carries kaymak begins here, at four in the morning.
cat.drinksNote: What is carried to the table beside the plate. Two of them are made here and take as long as any work in this catalogue. The rest arrive cold, in glass, without being asked twice.

catalog.close: Forty-two works, one measure. What is not in this catalogue is not made in this house.

10.story: A twist rolled twice: cream in the inner turns, chocolate in the outer. It is the most exacting piece in the section, and it is made only when it has been ordered.
10.aria: Read the story: Burma Katmer, Çikolatalı Kaymaklı
10.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Burma Katmer, Çikolatalı Kaymaklı, Rolled twice

11.story: It is rolled to the thickness of a reed and baked until it snaps rather than bends. It is the most delicate thing to leave the workshop, and the only piece we refuse to put in a box.
11.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Çubuk Katmer, The thickness of a reed

12.story: The sheet is brought into a ring, the chocolate is closed inside the join, and it is baked until the seam disappears entirely. It is meant to be eaten standing, by hand. The street has always eaten it that way.
12.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Çikolatalı Simit, A ring, with chocolate

13.story: The same ring is filled with cream taken that morning and closed before the sheet cools. Cream inside the dough does not survive into a second day, so it is made in short batches, twice a day.
13.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Kaymaklı Simit, A ring, with cream

14.story: Kadayıf drawn as fine as hair is wrapped around unsalted cheese from the same morning and turned on hammered copper over an open fire. No part of it can be prepared ahead, so it is ordered last and eaten first.
14.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Klasik Künefe, Copper, fire, strand

15.story: The kadayıf is woven like a mat instead of being pressed flat, so the fire reaches the cheese through the gaps rather than from the edge. It comes off the flame like a woven mat. That is exactly what the name means.
15.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Hasır Künefe, Woven like a mat

16.note: Lower in sugar, the same fire
16.story: It is built exactly as the classic, with stevia in place of the syrup. Sugar is the only thing removed. The copper, the cheese and the flame stay, and so does the time it takes.
16.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Stevia Künefe, Lower in sugar, the same fire

17.story: It sits deeper in the pan, wider across, and it arrives under a heavier crown of pistachio than the house usually allows. It is meant to be shared, and it comes to the table with more than one fork.
17.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Paşa Künefe, The pasha’s share

18.story: The kadayıf is cut short and crystalline, and it holds the light the way cut glass does. It is crisper than the classic and allows very little slow handling, because a short strand takes colour in seconds.

19.note: Crystal, with a vein of cream
19.story: A vein of water-buffalo cream runs through the middle of the billuriye, so the crystalline edge meets something soft every time. The contrast lasts only a few minutes. That is the whole reason it is served quickly.
19.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Billurzade, Crystal, with a vein of cream

20.story: It is buried under Antep pistachio, ground coarse so that each piece stays separate. The kadayıf underneath is barely visible, and that is the point: what you eat is the pistachio. The strand is only the method.

21.story: A single copper plate is divided down the middle: a mound of pistachio on one side, the woven mat on the other. It exists because the table could not decide. The two are worth arguing over more than explaining.
21.aria: Read the story: Yarım Fıstıkzade ve Yarım Hasır
21.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Yarım Fıstıkzade ve Yarım Hasır, Two halves, one plate

22.note: A new form, the old method
22.story: Two rounds of kadayıf close over cheese and pistachio, and the edges are pressed on the flame until they join. A new form, carrying an entirely old method. It is the house’s one real concession to the present.
22.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Burger Künefe, A new form, the old method

23.story: Fine kadayıf is buttered strand by strand and filled with pistachio before it meets the fire. It is baked slowly so the outside gilds while the centre stays soft. Hurry it, and the colour comes without the texture.
23.aria: Read the story: Fıstıklı Tel Kadayıf
23.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Fıstıklı Tel Kadayıf, Buttered, strand by strand

24.note: A crystal cut, on its own
24.story: The crystal cut leaves the copper pan and comes as a dish of its own: brittle, bright, and brought to the syrup only at the last moment. Held any longer, the whole point softens and disappears.
24.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Billuriye Kadayıf, A crystal cut, on its own

25.story: The mound of pistachio is laid over kadayıf rather than künefe: no cheese, no cream, nothing between the pistachio and the strand. It is the plainest work in the catalogue, and the hardest to hide behind.
25.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Fıstıkzade Kadayıf, Nothing between pistachio and strand

26.story: Forty sheets of yufka, each opened thin enough to be read through like a printed page, are layered with clarified butter and chosen Antep pistachio. It bakes in copper, rests, and meets the syrup at the exact difference in heat that keeps the leaves apart.
26.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Fıstıklı Baklava, Forty leaves of light

27.story: The baklava is cut long and narrow instead of in the usual diamond, which changes both the path of the syrup between the leaves and the way a corner breaks on the fork. The same tray, read differently.
27.aria: Read the story: Özel Dilim Baklava
27.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Özel Dilim Baklava, A particular slice

28.story: It rests in the cold and is finished with milk instead of syrup. It is a summer dish, and the only baklava in the house that is not eaten hot. What keeps the leaves apart is the cold, not the sugar.
28.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Soğuk Baklava, Cold, with milk

29.story: It is cut from the block with a heated knife. Salep and mastic are turned slowly enough to hold a square edge. That is the only honest test of whether it was made properly.
29.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Sade Dilim, With a hot knife

30.story: The same slice leans on a vein of pistachio paste, ground in the house to a coarse, oily green. The paste is never sweetened. It is there for weight and colour, not for sugar.
30.aria: Read the story: Fıstık Ezmeli Dilim
30.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Fıstık Ezmeli Dilim, A vein of pistachio paste

31.story: The plain baton is pressed into the mould by hand and held at the only temperature that will keep its edge. Nothing is added. It is the base recipe, set in the middle so the others can be judged against it.
31.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Baton Sade, Pressed by hand

32.story: The baton is rolled in ground Antep pistachio until no white is left on the surface. It is done while the block is still firm, so the pistachio sits on the outside instead of being pressed in.
32.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Baton Fıstıklı, Rolled until no white remains

33.story: It is dipped in dark chocolate that sets hard against the cold and cracks cleanly at the first bite. The shell is thin on purpose: enough to snap, not enough to chew.
33.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Baton Çikolatalı, A shell that cracks

34.story: It is worked with a long-handled paddle until it stretches like dough and can hang from the arm without falling. Salep gives it that pull. It comes the old way: cut with a knife, not scooped.
34.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Kol Dondurma, Pulled by the arm

35.story: Water-buffalo milk is held on the lowest flame through the night, until the cream rises and settles as a single sheet. It is lifted at dawn, rolled, and comes with nothing but honey or pistachio. Anything more would be an argument with it.
35.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Süt Kaymak, Lifted at dawn

36.note: A foam that is not broken
36.story: It is ground to a powder and cooked slowly in a copper cezve so the foam rises once and is never broken. Water comes first, always. The coffee is reached with a clean mouth.
36.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Türk Kahvesi, A foam that is not broken

37.note: A slim glass, a double pot
37.story: It is brewed in a double pot and poured to the colour the guest asks for, from a deep red down to a pale amber. A slim glass, a saucer, two cubes of sugar beside it. It is not stirred for you.
37.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Çay, A slim glass, a double pot

38.story: It is kept in the coldest part of the refrigerator and opened at the table, not behind the counter. Glass bottles only. The house has never served a can, and has no intention of starting.
38.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Kola, Ice cold, in glass

39.note: With a slice, if you ask
39.story: Chilled, in glass, poured over ice, and with a slice of lemon if the table wants one. It cuts through a heavy plate of pistachio more cleanly than anything else on this list.
39.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Fanta, With a slice, if you ask

40.story: This is the drink the house sets against its sweetest plates, because it leaves nothing on the palate. Cold, clear, and deliberately alone.

41.story: Plain, or touched with lemon, and as cold as the refrigerator allows. This is what closes a heavy plate. Regulars ask for it before the meal is finished.

42.story: Still or sparkling, it is put on the table before a single order is taken. It is the first thing to arrive, and the only thing no one has to ask for.

01.story: The dough is thrown into the air until it is the width of a table and nearly transparent, then closed over water-buffalo cream and coarsely chopped Antep pistachio. It belongs to dawn: it is not held, not reheated, and not taken out of the room where it was made.
01.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Klasik Katmer, Opened at dawn

02.story: The same transparent sheet is folded into the triangle called muska. Inside there is nothing but water-buffalo cream and pistachio; the fold itself holds the close, not a seal.
02.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Kaymaklı Muska, A muska fold, with cream

03.story: The muska fold is given to dark chocolate that melts from nothing but the heat the stone has held. The corners stay crisp and the centre gives way. That is the whole reason it is eaten at once.
03.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Çikolatalı Muska, A muska fold, with chocolate

04.story: Inside a single fold, chocolate and water-buffalo cream sit in separate layers so that neither overwhelms the other. The sheet between them is what keeps both readable.
04.aria: Read the story: Çikolatalı Kaymaklı Muska
04.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Çikolatalı Kaymaklı Muska, The two, kept apart

05.story: Belgian couverture is tempered and spread in one thin coat before the fold is closed. It is darker than the house chocolate, and plainly richer, so the pistachio is held back on purpose.
05.aria: Read the story: Belçika Çikolatalı Muska
05.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Belçika Çikolatalı Muska, Belgian couverture

06.story: White chocolate is set against the deep green of Antep pistachio — the only place the house allows a contrast this high. It is sweeter than everything around it, and it is deliberately the smallest portion we cut.
06.aria: Read the story: Beyaz Çikolatalı Muska
06.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Beyaz Çikolatalı Muska, White, against the green

07.story: Katmer laid for a table, not for one person: it is spread edge to edge on a copper tray and cut only at the moment it is carried out. The centre stays soft. The rim, against the metal, turns crisp.
07.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Tepsi Katmer, For a whole table

08.story: The sheet is rolled around a pin, gathered along its length and twisted. The cream is not spread on top; it is drawn through the folds, so it shows in the cut rather than on the surface.
08.aria: Read the story: Burma Katmer, Kaymaklı
08.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Burma Katmer, Kaymaklı, Rolled, cream drawn through

09.story: The same twist, this time wrapped around dark chocolate softened on the stone. Cut across, the spiral reads as a dark thread turning inside the pale sheet.
09.aria: Read the story: Burma Katmer, Çikolatalı
09.alt: Hançerlioğlu - Burma Katmer, Çikolatalı, Rolled, with chocolate
